$$ v = \sqrt{ \frac{G M}{r} } $$

This formula shows that **orbital velocity decreases as the distance from the center of mass increases** (i.e., $ v \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{r}} $). It also shows that **orbital velocity is independent of the mass of the orbiting object**, $ m $, which is an important distinction.

- Setting gravitational force equal to centripetal force:
